role: Explains what CI runs where: gates.yml (ubuntu) and ci.yml at scope unit on every pull request and push to main, the UI target and full coverage floors (scope full) on demand and before releases, make ci locally; the gate self-verification harnesses; and what the posture does not claim.

units.does: Claims every pull request and push to main runs gates.yml (bash/python gates including the code map, ubuntu, about a minute) and ci.yml at scope unit (SwiftLint and budgets, strict concurrency, macOS build, unit suite with the Views coverage floor, unit suite under Thread Sanitizer, jobs in parallel, a run taking 30 to 40 minutes because Thread Sanitizer and the tests job each take 20 to 40 minutes on a runner), and that main requires the gates.yml job and the five ci.yml jobs (named) to pass on a branch up to date with main before anything merges; public repositories pay no minutes for standard runners; the UI target and full coverage floors (scope full, about two hours on current runners) run on demand and before every release. Code: gates.yml and ci.yml trigger on pull_request and push to branches [main]; testflight.yml calls ci.yml. The required checks are a repository ruleset setting (ruleset "main requires gates": Script gates (no Xcode), Lint + tech-debt budgets, Strict concurrency enabled, Release build, Thread Sanitizer, Tests + coverage, branch up to date), not visible in the repo.

units.key: § CI posture > What actually enforces quality here
units.does: Claims `make ci` runs every gate, the Release build, the unit suite under Thread Sanitizer and the full test suite with the identical scripts and .ci budget files CI uses; that nothing records it ran; and that it differs from GitHub in running the tests at scope full and in comparing budgets with the merge base with origin/main rather than the parent commit or PR base. Makefile ci lists the static gates, verify-gates, release-build, thread-sanitizer and test-coverage (TEST_SCOPE defaults to full); budget-monotonicity uses the origin/main merge base; ci.yml's baseline step uses HEAD~1 and gates.yml the PR base or push-before tip.

units.key: § CI posture > What actually enforces quality here > Running CI locally before pushing
units.does: Claims make ci-local (scope gates) / ci-local-unit (scope unit, adding the Release build, unit suite and Thread Sanitizer) run scripts/simulate_ci.sh, which parses ci.yml and executes its run: blocks in order, treating unknown steps as errors, choosing jobs by evaluating each job's `if:` against the scope, and skipping only Xcode selection and the SwiftLint install onto the runner's PATH; should run after committing because the ratchet compares HEAD to HEAD~1. Makefile ci-local/ci-local-unit call simulate_ci.sh (with --scope unit); simulate_ci.sh loads ci.yml via yaml.safe_load, job_runs() evaluates `inputs.X ==/!= 'v'`, and its skip patterns match sudo xcode-select and $GITHUB_PATH (plus brew install, which ci.yml no longer uses).

units.key: § CI posture > What actually enforces quality here > The gates
units.does: Claims the listed gate groups (Style & debt including the tech-debt budgets with the Watch target against its combined ceiling and whole-number ceilings; a Supply chain row whose last gate is every xcodebuild run pinned to Package.resolved; a Change tracking row for the code map, where a record whose callee changed fails the check until it is re-read) are all scripts in scripts/ run by make ci, make ci-local and Actions, with only the budget ratchet's baseline differing; every gate except check_coverage.sh (NEEDS_BUILD) has a plant in verify_gates_fail.sh, check_thread_sanitizer.sh's plants running it against a stand-in xcodebuild (race_in_suite, parallel_testing_hides_races, race_does_not_fail_run) and the gate itself first requiring the ThreadSanitizerCanaryTests race to be reported and fail its run; the meta-check enumerates scripts/check_*.sh and enforce_*.sh failing on any without a plant or exemption; check_budget_monotonicity.sh skips without a baseline, make budget-monotonicity passes the merge base with origin/main (or HEAD, saying so) overridable by BUDGET_BASE_REF, ci.yml compares with the parent commit and gates.yml with the PR base or push-before tip.
calls: .github/workflows/ci.yml::step lint-and-budgets/Every gate is wired into CI

units.key: § CI posture > What actually enforces quality here > Three questions, not one
units.does: Claims each gate is checked three ways: verify_gates_fail.sh (goes red), check_gate_preflight.sh (fails closed), check_gates_wired.sh (wired into ci.yml). All three scripts exist; ci.yml has 'Gates actually fail', 'Gates fail closed' and 'Every gate is wired into CI' steps.
calls: .github/workflows/ci.yml::step lint-and-budgets/Every gate is wired into CI

units.key: § CI posture > What actually enforces quality here > Two things must not read the tree at the same time
units.does: Claims verify_gates_fail.sh and verify_tests_fail.sh mutate tracked source and restore in an EXIT trap, both take .git/emuqu-tree-mutation.lock, simulate_ci.sh refuses to start while it is held, and a stale lock is taken over with a warning; check_no_leaked_mutations.sh is the backstop for a killed run. Code: both harnesses source scripts/lib/preflight.sh and call gate_acquire_tree_lock (verify_gates_fail.sh, verify_tests_fail.sh) with release in the EXIT trap; GATE_TREE_LOCK defaults to <git dir>/emuqu-tree-mutation.lock (falling back to TMPDIR when no git dir); simulate_ci.sh calls gate_require_unmutated_tree; preflight.sh warns on a stale lock.

units.key: § CI posture > What actually enforces quality here > The tests are checked too, not just the code
units.does: Claims verify_tests_fail.sh mutates a chosen set of behaviours (pNN50 threshold, SDNN, RMSSD, NP fourth root, recovery label comparison, encrypted-write branch) and requires the suite to catch each; logic lifted out of large types gets its own mutations; TrackBackupWatermark's test drops one cursor at a time with a mutation per clause, and the recovery merge's more-beats tie-break is its own function with its own test because DataSourceSelector answers first. verify_tests_fail.sh defines mutate(), a pnn50_threshold mutation of TimeDomainAnalysis 'abs($0) > 50' -> 75 against EmuquTests/TimeDomainTests, and TrackBackupWatermark mutations.

units.key: § CI posture > What actually enforces quality here > Where to point it next: at the comments that claim something is subtle
units.does: Claims comments that call behaviour subtle are mutation leads: tests pin the three RRDataImporter+CSV.rrValue asymmetries with permanent mutations; WorkoutMileMarkerEngine's zone label must use max HR, not session peak, as the denominator, with tests and a mutation swapping it back; the delete accompanying every Apple Health re-export is HealthSampleReplacer's (read earlier own samples, save, delete the earlier ones notReplacedBySync), and its naming scheme HealthExportIdentity has tests asserting no metric's delete reaches another metric's or session's samples; verify_tests_fail.sh needs a build per mutation so it is not in make ci.

units.key: § CI posture > What actually enforces quality here > Runs are scoped, because a full one is expensive
units.does: Says ci.yml takes a dispatch scope with approximate billable minutes at macOS rates (a public repository is not billed for these runners): gates (dispatch default, lint/budgets/strict concurrency, ~14), unit (+ unit suite and Thread Sanitizer, ~300), full (+ UI target and coverage floors, ~1080); the UI target is 66 of the tests job's 88 minutes; pull requests and pushes run unit; workflow_call defaults to full so the TestFlight deploy gate checks a release against everything. Code: ci.yml workflow_dispatch input scope default gates with those options; pull_request/push carry no inputs, so the scope != 'gates' jobs run and tests takes TEST_SCOPE unit; workflow_call input scope default full; testflight.yml quality-gate uses ./.github/workflows/ci.yml.

units.key: § CI posture > What actually enforces quality here > The compiler is one of the gates
units.does: Claims run_tests_with_coverage.sh passes -warn-long-expression-type-checking and -warn-long-function-bodies, the spec-conformance scan covers the whole app target (including Emuqu/EmuquApp.swift, where verify_gates_fail.sh plants a violation), there are zero swiftlint:disable directives in Emuqu/Sources, and check_budget_monotonicity.sh fails unjustified raises. Code: run_tests_with_coverage.sh TYPE_CHECK_FLAGS with =4000/=6000; grep finds 0 swiftlint:disable in Emuqu/Sources.

units.key: § CI posture > Where GitHub Actions is still used
units.does: Claims every pull request and push to main runs gates.yml and ci.yml (unit), testflight.yml calls ci.yml as a reusable workflow at scope full, its deploy job runs in the testflight environment (main only, owner approval per run, holds the signing and App Store Connect secrets), its own if: also requires refs/heads/main, and its 'Remove signing material' step (if: always()) deletes the keychain and keys; security.yml (CodeQL and dependency review) is on demand, the review failing unless every Package.resolved pin is in the dependency-graph SBOM ('Require the Swift packages in the dependency graph'). The environment's branch rule and reviewer are repository settings, not visible in the repo.
calls: .github/workflows/security.yml::step dependency-review/Require the Swift packages in the dependency graph

units.key: § CI posture > What this posture does *not* claim
units.does: Claims a pull request gets the macOS build, unit suite with the Views floor and Thread Sanitizer, while the UI flows and overall/logic coverage floors run only at scope full (on demand and before a release), so a UI-only break can reach main; and that the UI flows are not a required check: main requires the gates.yml job and the five ci.yml jobs at scope unit (lint and budgets, strict concurrency, the Release build, Thread Sanitizer, tests with coverage). Code: ci.yml tests job TEST_SCOPE unit unless scope full. The required check is a repository ruleset setting (ruleset "main requires gates": Script gates (no Xcode), Lint + tech-debt budgets, Strict concurrency enabled, Release build, Thread Sanitizer, Tests + coverage, branch up to date), not visible in the repo.

Tells reviewers the macOS build, unit suite and Thread Sanitizer run on every pull request and push to main and the UI target on demand and before a release; main requires six checks on a branch up to date with it, the Linux gates.yml job and the five ci.yml jobs; for evidence, look at the CI run on the pull request or commit, whose run summary has one line per macOS job with scope and result, and ask for a scope full run for the UI target; Claims evidence_report.sh prints enforced ceilings (--json for machine output) without builds; sbom.spdx.json covers the app plus 11 resolved packages and make sbom-check fails when stale; the SBOM is unsigned with no build provenance. Code: ci.yml summary steps in thread-sanitizer and tests; sbom.spdx.json has 12 packages (app + 11); Makefile sbom-check. The required checks are a repository ruleset setting (ruleset "main requires gates": Script gates (no Xcode), Lint + tech-debt budgets, Strict concurrency enabled, Release build, Thread Sanitizer, Tests + coverage, branch up to date), not visible in the repo.
calls: .github/workflows/ci.yml::step thread-sanitizer/Write the result to the run summary
.github/workflows/ci.yml::step tests/Write the result to the run summary
